chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn Qurti, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Maintaining good relations with relatives improves character, makes the hand generous, purifies the soul, increases sustenance, and delays death.

key_terms.تُسَمِّحُ الْكَفَّ: Makes the hand generous / Encourages giving
key_terms.صِلَةُ الْأَرْحَامِ: Maintaining kinship ties / Good relations with relatives

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and worldly benefits of maintaining good relations with relatives in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the holistic impact of silat al-arham, linking social cohesion to individual spiritual and physical well-being. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on kinship not merely as a social duty but as a means of divine grace that refines character (khuluq) and extends life (ajal), reflecting the interconnectedness of the spiritual and material realms.
